title: Design System: Hannah · German lessons in Abu Dhabi

article.purpose: The der/die/das word in every section lockup; the largest recurring type.

display.purpose: The single h1 and the closing line.

noun.purpose: The German noun beside the article in a lockup.

headline.purpose: The English gloss under a section lockup, carrying the SEO heading text.

title.purpose: Step titles, door links, FAQ questions, price-row formats.

label.purpose: Nav links, table headers, skill tags, fine print.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single easing for every transition and the load wipe.

motion.name: field-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0) over 0.9s, staggered 0 / 0.12s / 0.24s
motion.purpose: Hero fields wipe in once on load along the article order der, die, das. Off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: quiz-flood
motion.value: clip-path circle(0%) to circle(150%) at the tapped tile over 0.75s
motion.purpose: The correct article's colour floods the quiz strip.

motion.name: arrow-nudge
motion.purpose: Arrows in buttons and doors slide right on hover.

narrative.overview:
Every German learner memorises nouns with a colour: der blue, die rose, das green. This system turns that classroom code into the whole visual language. Each section is a German noun, and its grammatical article decides its colour, so colour always carries meaning and never decorates. The page is built from full-bleed flat fields of those three colours, indigo ink and white paper, divided by 2px ink rules and set in a heavy, tightly tracked grotesque.

The density is generous and confident: big type, long rules, few elements per field. Depth comes only from colour fields meeting at hard edges, never from shadow, gradient or rounding. Motion is short and purposeful: the three hero fields wipe in once along the article order, and the quiz floods its strip with the right article's colour.

The user's steer rules out the German flag palette completely. No black, red or gold appears anywhere; the darkest value is indigo ink.
keyCharacteristics: Colour is grammar: der blue, die rose, das green, chosen by each section's noun.
Full-bleed flat fields with hard edges; no radius, shadow or gradient anywhere.
Every section header is a lockup: the article huge, the German noun beside it, an English gloss below.
2px ink rules structure lists, tables and accordions.
Bricolage Grotesque at 700 to 800 for display; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for reading.

rules.name: The Article Decides Rule
rules.body: A section's colour comes from its German noun's grammatical gender, never from taste. Name the noun first, then take the colour: der → blue, die → rose, das → green. A new section with no fitting noun stays on paper.

rules.name: The No Flag Rule
rules.body: No black, red or gold, ever, not even as an accent, tint or hover. The darkest value in the system is Indigo Ink.

rules.name: The Ink on Light Fields Rule
rules.body: Text on die rose and das green is ink; text on der blue is white. On paper, a coloured article uses its deepened "on paper" value, never the field value.

rules.name: The Lockup Rule
rules.body: Every section header is a lockup: the article in Article type, the noun beside it on the same baseline, the English gloss on its own line beneath. German words carry `lang="de"`.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Display type is Bricolage at 700 or 800 only; reading text is Atkinson at 400, with 700 for emphasis. Never set paragraphs in Bricolage.

rules.name: The Flat Field Rule
rules.body: Separate things with a colour change or a 2px rule, never with a shadow or a gradient.

dos: **Do** pick every coloured section's field by its German noun's article: der #2f5fd0, die #e86fa5, das #33a873.
**Do** set every section header as an article + noun + gloss lockup, with `lang="de"` on the German.
**Do** use ink (#1b2547) text on die rose and das green, and white text on der blue.
**Do** use the deepened values (die #c13f7c, das #1f7d52) when an article colour is text on white.
**Do** structure lists, tables and accordions with 2px rules.
**Do** keep every corner square and every surface flat.
**Do** use cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) for transitions, and turn off the field wipe and smooth scroll under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: **Don't** use black, red or gold anywhere, including tints, hovers, shadows or illustrations. Those are the German flag colours and the user ruled them out.
**Don't** use a gender colour for decoration or for a section whose noun has a different article.
**Don't** add border radius, drop shadows or gradients.
**Don't** set body paragraphs in Bricolage Grotesque.
**Don't** put white text on die rose or das green.
